Issues.Title: Fix DataFrame GroupBy Min, Max, Product and Sum aggregations
Issues.Body:
The row-subset overloads of the numeric `Min`, `Max`, `Product` and `Sum` computations (the ones `GroupBy` uses) had several problems:

- `Product(rows)` started from `default`, so it always returned 0.
- None of them checked the null bitmap, so nulls were treated as their zero-filled storage (e.g. `Min` of `[5, null]` returned 0).
- An empty or all-null selection returned `MaxValue`/`MinValue`/0 instead of null.
- `DateTime` `Min(rows)`/`Max(rows)` initialized a nullable result to null and compared against it with lifted operators, so they always returned null.

Changes:

- `PrimitiveDataFrameColumnComputations.tt`: the row-subset `Min`/`Max`/`Sum`/`Product` now skip null rows (reading the matching null bitmap buffer). `Min`/`Max`/`Sum` return null when no valid value was seen, the same as the whole-column overloads. `Product` starts from 1 and, like the whole-column `Product`, returns 1 for an empty selection. I regenerated `PrimitiveDataFrameColumnComputations.cs` from the template.
- `DateTimeComputation.cs`: `Min(rows)`/`Max(rows)` now track a `hasValue` flag and skip nulls, like the whole-column versions.

I left the existing `checked` arithmetic in the row-subset overloads alone. Because `Product` now returns real values, the existing `TestGroupBy` needed an update: it had asserted a product of 0 for both groups. The odd group's product is 189, which overflows `sbyte`, so the test now leaves the `Sbyte` column out of that `Product` call.

The indexed `Cumulative*` issues mentioned in the issue comments are not part of this change.

Testing:

- Added `DataFrameGroupByTests.TestGroupByMinMaxProductSum`. It covers groups with nulls, positive and negative values, an all-null group, and DateTime Min/Max. It fails before the fix and passes after.
- `dotnet test test/Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests` (net8.0, macOS arm64): 1765 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed.

Fixes #5704

Issues.Title: SymSGD classification test hangs on Linux ARM32 Helix
Issues.Body:
**System Information (please complete the following information):**
- OS & Version: Ubuntu 22.04 ARM32 Helix container (`ubuntu-22.04-helix-arm32v7`).
- ML.NET Version: PR #7833, commit `100af589f`.
- .NET Version: .NET 8, Debug and Release.

**Describe the bug**
`TestEstimatorSymSgdClassificationTrainer` becomes runnable with accurate native-library detection, then reports `Too many args to microtask: 26!` and hangs until the 3,600-second work-item timeout. Debug also reports `malloc(): unsorted double linked list corrupted`.

**Screenshots, Code, Sample Projects**
[Debug log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/7834abec-17f1-4f70-9f01-fbcbe491ac4e/workitems/Microsoft.ML.Tests/console) · [Release log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/a50b77ad-04db-47be-8087-a5eca6a0e69e/workitems/Microsoft.ML.Tests/console)

After the first quarantine, [build 1643911](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1643911) reaches `TestEstimatorSymSgdInitPredictor`, which reports the same microtask error and exits 255 ([Release log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/a5f3557f-2ac4-47ef-a3dd-b833078677fd/workitems/Microsoft.ML.Tests/console)). The recorded failures are from Helix; the quarantine is OS/architecture-based.

Issues.Title: TensorFlow image classification tests running out of memory on Linux x64
Issues.Body:
**System Information (please complete the following information):**
- OS & Version: Ubuntu 22.04 and CentOS Stream 9 x64 Helix containers.
- ML.NET Version: PR #7833, commit `100af589f`.
- .NET Version: .NET 8, Debug and Release.

**Describe the bug**
Accurate native-library detection enables previously skipped TensorFlow tests. The process exits with code 137 during `TensorFlowImageClassificationWithExponentialLRScheduling` in Release and `TensorFlowImageClassificationBadImages` in Debug. Debug logs report peak memory up to 7.2 GB. An OOM kill is suspected, not kernel-confirmed.

**Screenshots, Code, Sample Projects**
[Ubuntu Debug log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/3dd9ea81-c306-4655-a8c0-e70cb5043a59/workitems/Microsoft.ML.TensorFlow.Tests/console) · [Ubuntu Release log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/b7513017-c96f-4c53-9973-1e01da19c7ec/workitems/Microsoft.ML.TensorFlow.Tests/console)

**Additional context**
Temporarily quarantine the six image-classification training methods (10 test cases) as a group on Linux x64, including local runs and both build configurations. This covers default training, architecture variants, learning-rate scheduling, early stopping, and bad images. Keep non-training TensorFlow tests and other platforms enabled.

Reproduced outside Helix in Ubuntu 22.04 WSL x64 with the original Release binaries, .NET 8.0.16 and two CPUs: at a 16 GiB limit, 36 tests passed with 2 existing skips (peak RSS about 14.2 GiB). At an experimental 8 GiB limit, the kernel OOM-killed `dotnet` during `BadImages`. This does not establish the actual Helix memory limit. Memory retention across tests may contribute, so individual skips may only move the failure later.

The two initial skips were honored, but [build 1643911](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1643911) was killed later in `TensorFlowImageClassification` or `TensorFlowImageClassificationEarlyStopping` ([Ubuntu Release log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/f9c5c2bb-6518-4b8d-aab6-2dc6cd82ac29/workitems/Microsoft.ML.TensorFlow.Tests/console)). The latest payload also OOM-kills at 8 GiB in WSL. Enabling the existing per-test GC option did not prevent the OOM, so that experiment was reverted.

With the training-group quarantine, the same 8 GiB WSL reproduction completes successfully: 26 passed and 8 reported skips (6 training methods plus 2 existing model-unavailable skips), with peak RSS about 1.26 GiB. The two quarantined theories cover multiple data rows. Linux CI still needs to rerun; this is a temporary coverage reduction, not a fix for the memory retention.

Issues.Title: Document the public API review and approval process
Issues.Body:
Make it explicit that every public API addition, modification or removal in a package built from this repository requires maintainer approval recorded in a GitHub issue before implementation or opening an implementation PR.

The process follows dotnet/runtime's API review approach, adapted for ML.NET ownership and its existing review labels.

## Changes

- Document proposal requirements, review stages, recorded approval with `api-approved`, breaking-change considerations, and renewed approval when the design changes.
- Clarify that protected APIs and APIs in preview or experimental packages also require review.
- Keep exploratory prototypes and draft PRs in contributors' own forks while proposals are under review.
- Add an API proposal issue template and direct relevant feature requests to it.
- Update both contributor guides, the documentation index, PR checklist and Copilot instructions to reference the process.

This is a documentation and template change only. It does not change product APIs, introduce automated enforcement, or create GitHub labels.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Document the public API review and approval process" (#7821)

Issues.Title: Preserve row order for equal DataFrame sort keys
Issues.Body:
Fixes #6443.

`DataFrame.OrderBy` can reorder rows with equal keys, so a subsequent sort loses the ordering established by a previous one. Sorting strings across multiple buffers can also throw when a buffer's next value is already present in the merge dictionary.

Use the original row index to break value ties throughout the existing introsort implementation. Reverse the internal tie order for descending output, which is filled backwards. Keep equal-value merge candidates ordered by buffer index, combine candidates sharing a value, and collect null row indices in their original order. The protected merge API remains unchanged.

Regression tests compare output row IDs with LINQ's stable ordering for primitive and string columns, both sort directions and null placements, and strings spanning multiple buffers. Additional partitioned-input cases exercise larger duplicate-key inputs. The 12 initial scenarios all failed before the fix and pass with it.

Validation on Windows:

- DataFrame test project, Release / net8.0: 1,784 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- DataFrame test project, Release / net48 and net9.0: 1,784 passed per target, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Each target was run with `dotnet test test/Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests/Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests.csproj -c Release -f <target> /p:TestTargetFramework=<target>`.
- Ran the required repository-root build first. It could not complete because the native C++/CMake prerequisites are unavailable; the DataFrame managed build and tests succeed.

- [x] There's a descriptive title that will make sense to other developers some time from now.
- [x] There's an associated issue.
- [x] The description explains the change and approach.
- [x] Necessary tests are included.

Issues.Title: AutoML BinaryClassificationExperiment.Execute throws NullReferenceException in ConcatenateEntity.ToString when ColumnInformation names a column the preFeaturizer creates
Issues.Body:
### System information

- Microsoft.ML 5.0.1, Microsoft.ML.AutoML 0.23.1
- .NET 10 (net10.0), macOS arm64

### Describe the bug

`BinaryClassificationExperiment.Execute(trainData, columnInformation, preFeaturizer)` throws a `NullReferenceException` from `ConcatenateEntity.ToString` when `ColumnInformation` names a column that the preFeaturizer creates. It does not report that the column does not exist.

### To reproduce

```csharp
var pre = ml.Transforms.Text.TokenizeIntoCharactersAsKeys("text__chars", "text")
    .Append(ml.Transforms.Text.ProduceNgrams("text__counts", "text__chars", 4));
var info = new ColumnInformation { LabelColumnName = "label" };
info.IgnoredColumnNames.Add("text");
info.NumericColumnNames.Add("text__counts");          // created by the preFeaturizer
ml.Auto().CreateBinaryClassificationExperiment(new BinaryExperimentSettings { MaxExperimentTimeInSeconds = 10 })
  .Execute(train, info, pre);
```

```
System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
   at Microsoft.ML.AutoML.ConcatenateEntity.ToString()
   at Microsoft.ML.AutoML.SweepablePipeline..ctor(...)
   at Microsoft.ML.AutoML.SweepablePipeline.AppendEntity(...)
   at Microsoft.ML.AutoML.SweepableExtension.Append(IEstimator`1 estimator, SweepablePipeline pipeline)
   at Microsoft.ML.AutoML.BinaryClassificationExperiment.CreateBinaryClassificationPipeline(IDataView trainData, ColumnInformation columnInformation, IEstimator`1 preFeaturizer)
```

The featurizer is built from `trainData`'s schema before the preFeaturizer runs, so a column the preFeaturizer adds is not found. If the preFeaturizer writes its output back under an existing column name (for example `NormalizeLpNorm("text", …)` with `"text"` listed as numeric), training works.

### Expected behavior

One of:
- the pipeline is built from the preFeaturizer's output schema, so `ColumnInformation` can name columns the preFeaturizer produces, or
- `Execute` fails with a message naming the missing column.

Issues.Title: ONNX export of a reloaded NgramExtractingTransformer (useAllLengths: true) writes min_gram_length = ngramLength — the exported graph counts only the longest n-grams
Issues.Body:
### System information

- Microsoft.ML 5.0.1, Microsoft.ML.OnnxConverter 0.23.1, Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime 1.31.0
- .NET 10 (net10.0), macOS arm64

### Describe the bug

An `NgramExtractingTransformer` created with `useAllLengths: true` exports to ONNX correctly when it is converted straight after `Fit`. After a `Model.Save` / `Model.Load` round trip, the same transformer exports a `TfIdfVectorizer` node with `min_gram_length` equal to `max_gram_length`. The resulting graph counts only the longest n-grams. The conversion reports success, so nothing shows that the graph is wrong.

### To reproduce

Text column of the UCI SMS Spam Collection (4,459 training rows, 1,115 compared):

```csharp
var t = ml.Transforms.Text.TokenizeIntoCharactersAsKeys("c", "text")
    .Append(ml.Transforms.Text.ProduceNgrams("text", "c", ngramLength: 4, useAllLengths: true,
        weighting: NgramExtractingEstimator.WeightingCriteria.Tf))
    .Fit(train);
```

The `text` output vector (width 75,141) from ML.NET, compared with the same output of the exported graph run in ONNX Runtime:

| | rows that differ |
|---|---|
| `t` exported directly (`ml.Model.ConvertToOnnx(t, train, stream, "text")`) | **0 / 1,115** |
| `ml.Model.Save(t, …)` → `ml.Model.Load(…)` → export | **1,115 / 1,115** |

In the graph of the reloaded transformer, the `TfIdfVectorizer` node has `min_gram_length: 4, max_gram_length: 4` while `ngram_counts` is `[0, 112, 6500, 59291]`. The pool holds 1-, 2-, 3- and 4-grams, but only 4-grams are counted, so every 1–3-gram slot is 0. A logistic regression trained on these features scores every row of the reloaded export at about its intercept (probability ≈ 0.0017; ML.NET gives 0.0000–1.0000).

Workaround: use one `ProduceNgrams` per length (`useAllLengths: false`, lengths 1..4) followed by `Concatenate`. This exports correctly after a reload.

### Expected behavior

The exported `min_gram_length` is 1 when `useAllLengths` is true, whether or not the transformer went through `Model.Save` / `Model.Load`. In other words, the all-lengths setting survives deserialization in what the ONNX save path reads.

### Why it matters

Models are usually exported from a saved file (train → save → export later). In that path the conversion succeeds and the graph silently produces different values. Only a value-by-value comparison catches it.

Issues.Title: AutoML BinaryClassificationExperiment ignores ColumnInformation.ExampleWeightColumnName — trainers are fitted unweighted
Issues.Body:
### System information

- Microsoft.ML 5.0.0, Microsoft.ML.AutoML 0.23.0
- .NET 10 (net10.0), macOS arm64

### Describe the bug

`ColumnInformation.ExampleWeightColumnName` is accepted by `BinaryClassificationExperiment.Execute`, but the weight column does not reach the trainers the experiment builds, nor its validation metrics. No warning is emitted, so the caller gets an unweighted model while believing it is weighted.

### To reproduce

Fixture: 1,000 `X` values in [0,1] (plus a noise column `Y`), each row written twice — once `Label=true`, once `Label=false` — with weight `W = 10` / `1` for true / false when `X > 0.5`, and `1` / `10` otherwise. Unweighted, the label is independent of `X` (P = 0.5 everywhere); weighted, P(true | X=0.9) ≈ 0.9.

1. AutoML (15 s budget):
   ```csharp
   ml.Auto().CreateBinaryClassificationExperiment(15).Execute(train, new ColumnInformation
   {
       LabelColumnName = "Label",
       ExampleWeightColumnName = "W",
       NumericColumnNames = { "X", "Y" },
   });
   ```
   Best run `LbfgsLogisticRegressionBinary`: **P(true | X=0.9) = 0.49, P(true | X=0.1) = 0.49** — identical to the same experiment with `W` placed in `IgnoredColumnNames`. The per-trainer best validation AUCs were also identical in both runs (FastTree 0.41, FastForest 0.40, SdcaLogisticRegression 0.50, LbfgsLogisticRegression 0.53).

2. The same trainer fitted directly:
   ```csharp
   ml.Transforms.Concatenate("Features", "X", "Y")
     .Append(ml.BinaryClassification.Trainers.LbfgsLogisticRegression(exampleWeightColumnName: "W"));
   ```
   gives **0.96 / 0.04**.

### Expected behavior

Either the trainers AutoML constructs receive `exampleWeightColumnName` (the binary, multiclass and regression trainers it sweeps all accept it), with validation metrics weighted the same way — or `Execute` refuses / warns when `ExampleWeightColumnName` is set, so a weighted request cannot silently produce an unweighted fit.

### Why it matters

Labels collected by importance sampling, or from sources of differing reliability, are trained with per-row weights. A silently unweighted fit learns the sampling bias, and nothing in the result tells the caller.

Related: #6708 (documentation of `ExampleWeightColumnName`).

Issues.Title: Treat tab, line feed and carriage return as whitespace and keep symbols in BertTokenizer
Issues.Body:
`BertTokenizer` now follows the basic tokenization of BERT and Hugging Face in two places:

- `BertNormalizer` turns `\t`, `\n` and `\r` into spaces instead of removing them, so `note\nbook` is `note book`, not `notebook`. It also removes format and private-use characters, as the text cleaning of BERT does, and keeps the characters that are not assigned in Unicode, which become `[UNK]`.
- `BertTokenizer` uses a new internal pre-tokenizer: every punctuation character is a token, with the definition of BERT (Unicode punctuation and every ASCII character that is not a letter, a digit or whitespace), and every other run of non-whitespace characters is a word. `BertNormalizer` sets apart the punctuation outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, which the pre-tokenizer can't match on UTF-16 code units. So ``$ + < = > ^ ` | ~`` are tokens, and `°`, `©` and emoji reach WordPiece, which finds them in the vocabulary or gives `[UNK]`. `PreTokenizer.CreateWordOrPunctuation` is unchanged.

The cases of both issues, and a few more, are in `BertTokenizerTests`, with the tokens Hugging Face `tokenizers` gives on the same vocabulary; they fail without the change. Compared with Hugging Face `tokenizers` 0.23.3, texts encoded to the same ids:

| Corpus | Texts | all-MiniLM-L6-v2 | bert-base-uncased | bert-base-cased |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| WikiText-103, test split, non-empty lines | 2,891 | 2,054 → 2,891 | 2,054 → 2,891 | 2,054 → 2,891 |
| XNLI, test split, premises in 15 languages | 75,150 | 69,627 → 75,150 | 69,627 → 75,150 | 69,630 → 75,150 |
| Source code in C#, Java, Python, C++ and TypeScript, blocks of 20 lines | 5,962 | 282 → 5,962 | 282 → 5,962 | 282 → 5,962 |
| Every code point from U+0000 to U+3FFFF and U+E0000 to U+E01EF, alone | 260,592 | 57,122 → 258,679 | 57,122 → 258,679 | 58,029 → 260,507 |
| Every punctuation and symbol code point between two words, as in `one§line` | 8,617 | 584 → 8,489 | 584 → 8,489 | 582 → 8,485 |

Options: `LowerCaseBeforeTokenization` and `RemoveNonSpacingMarks` on for the uncased models, off for the cased one.

No text that had the same ids as Hugging Face before has different ids now, except U+1734 alone with the uncased models: .NET classifies it as a spacing mark and the Unicode tables of `tokenizers` as a non-spacing one, which accent stripping removes. The code points that still differ are mostly Hangul syllables and combining marks with `RemoveNonSpacingMarks`, and characters assigned in recent Unicode versions, as the punctuation added after Unicode 8.0, which `tokenizers` does not treat as punctuation; they are outside these two issues.

Fixes #7724
Fixes #7725

Issues.Title: Split buffers by target type capacity when cloning primitive columns
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7381

`PrimitiveColumnContainer<T>.CloneAs*Container` mapped every source buffer to exactly one buffer of the target type. Buffer capacity is `ArrayUtility.ArrayMaxSize / sizeof(T)`, so this breaks in two ways:

- When the target type is larger (e.g. `int` -> `double`), a full source buffer holds more values than a target buffer can. Cloning an `Int32DataFrameColumn` with more than ~268M values as double threw `ArgumentException: ... exceeds buffer capacity`. This is reachable from public APIs like `Int32DataFrameColumn.Add(double)`.
- When the target type is smaller (e.g. `long` -> `int`), the result contains buffers that aren't full. Row lookups assume every buffer except the last holds exactly `MaxCapacity` values (`rowIndex / MaxCapacity`), so indexing into that result returns the wrong values.

### Fix

The per-type copy loops are replaced with one private `CloneAs<U>(Func<T, U> convert)` helper. It fills target buffers up to `ReadOnlyDataFrameBuffer<U>.MaxCapacity` and starts a new buffer and null bitmap when one is full. Validity bits are copied into the matching new bitmap. When the column has no nulls they are set in bulk. Each `CloneAs*Container` method now just passes its converter to this helper. For `bool`, values from a non-bool column still become `false` and the validity bits are kept, as before.

### Testing

- Added `PrimitiveDataFrameColumn_Int32_CloneAsDouble_AcrossMultipleBuffers`. It builds an `Int32DataFrameColumn` that spans two buffers, calls `Add(0.5)` (which clones as double) and checks values and nulls around the double and int buffer boundaries. It is marked `X64Fact` like the other large-allocation tests next to it. For local runs on arm64 I temporarily switched it to `[Fact]`: it failed before the change with the `exceeds buffer capacity` exception and passes after it.
- `dotnet test test/Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests` passes: 1765 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed.
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` reports no changes for the touched files.

Issues.Title: Fix FeaturizeText failure when the n-gram dictionary is empty
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7529

If every row of the text column is empty, or contains only stop words that the stop word remover strips out, the word/char n-gram dictionaries end up empty. `NgramExtractingTransformer` then outputs a `VectorDataViewType` of size 0, which counts as variable-size. `TextFeaturizingEstimator.Fit` passes that column to `LpNormNormalizingTransformer`, which only accepts known-size vectors, so it throws:

```
Schema mismatch for input column 'Text_CharExtractor': expected Expected known-size vector of Single, got Vector<Single>
```

This happens with the default `Norm` (L2). With `Norm = None`, the same data already fits fine.

### Changes

- `TextFeaturizingEstimator.Fit`: only add the LpNorm step for an extractor output column when its type is valid for LpNorm (`LpNormNormalizingEstimatorBase.IsColumnTypeValid`). An empty n-gram vector has no slots, so there is nothing to normalize. Skipping the step means the default-norm case now behaves like the `Norm = None` case: `Fit` succeeds and the output column holds empty vectors.
- `ColumnConcatenatingTransformer`: in the sparse concatenation path, `Contracts.Assert(offset < dstLength)` fails in debug builds when a source vector has zero length (here, both the char and word vectors are empty, so `dstLength` is 0). A zero-length source is valid input, so the assert is now `offset <= dstLength`. Release behavior is unchanged.

### Testing

- Added `TextFeaturizerWithEmptyNgramDictionaryTest`, which covers both scenarios from the issue (all-empty strings, and stop-words-only text) with and without the char extractor. All three cases failed with the exception above before the change and pass after it.
- Ran the `TextFeaturizerTests`, `WordBagTransformerTests`, `NormalizerTests` and `ConcatTests` classes, plus all tests matching `Text`/`Concat`/`LpNorm`/`Ngram` in `Microsoft.ML.Tests`, on net8.0 (macOS arm64). All passed.

Local `actionlint`, workflow configuration, stage-routing, and data-guard checks passed. No model training or live labeling was run.

No automatic labeling or scheduled jobs are enabled. The new manual workflows must be on `main` before runtime testing; then use staged training and dry-run prediction before enabling writes.
